## Description
The immutable source-bound [Full Regression Run #42818385173](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/42818385173) for auto Staging convergence [PR #3192](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/pull/3192) completed with **one flaky case**: `terminal-io.spec.ts:1195` "a transport disconnect cancels the armed pad and stops its clock". First attempt timed out at line 1242 waiting 30 seconds for transient `terminal-connecting` UI; retry passed. The Full per-ID attestor explicitly requires `stats.flaky === 0`, so this regression can block automatic convergence even after the independent Project Select deterministic failure (#3199) is fixed.

## Reproduction
On the real Chromium Full stack, arm a direction-pad touch gesture, send ArrowUp, enable browser offline, close the tracked live /ws socket, and require `terminal-connecting` to become visible. That UI phase may be absent or too short to be observed while the actual transport disconnect and gesture cancellation can still be independently verified.

## Impact
The test's transient-banner assertion is a race-prone proxy for the actual safety property: **the connection must truly break, the armed touch pad must cancel immediately, no further ArrowUp repeats may be generated, and service recovers after online restoration**. Do not allow a passing but unobserved transport disconnect to satisfy the test.

## Root Cause
The test at `terminal-io.spec.ts:1195` uses a transient `terminal-connecting` DOM banner as a proxy for verifying WebSocket disconnect behavior. This banner may appear too briefly or be absent entirely during the actual transport disconnect, creating a race condition that causes timeouts even when the underlying safety property (armed pad cancellation, no new input, recovery) is correctly implemented.

## Fix Direction
- Before teardown, capture actual live /ws WebSocket instances and fail if none are open, then explicitly close them with the offline context active.
- Confirm those **same targeted socket instances** enter a terminal CLOSED state; fail if the network event never happened. Replace the fragile requirement that a transient `terminal-connecting` DOM banner must render.
- Preserve the required pad disappearance while the touch remains down, 1.3-second no-new-input guarantee, and recovered interactive shell after online restoration. Assert no false teardown/return success.
- Execute existing `terminal-io` regression in authenticated CI and verify a fresh canonical Full run has zero flaky, zero skipped, zero failed tests, not merely a retried successful case.

## Location
`e2e/tests/browser/terminal-io.spec.ts` (existing Test ID `terminal-io`). Do not change runtime gesture, network transport or required Full E2E gate without a separately reproduced product defect.

### Success Criteria
- [x] SC-01 A genuine browser /ws disconnect (at least one initially OPEN socket, exact socket(s) observed CLOSED) cancels armed pad and repeat, and the restored connection is interactive; browser regression verifies it without relying on a transient banner.
- [x] SC-02 A new source-bound Full Regression run for the next integration SHA shows `unexpected=0`, `skipped=0`, `flaky=0` with the exact per-ID attestation and preserves all other required checks; the previous failure is not turned into Pass.

**SC → scenario:** SC-01=SCN-02 real Chromium+WebSocket IO; SC-02=SCN-05 independently authenticated exact Full E2E Run/Job and per-ID receipt. Real network state and canonical suite required, not model/agent opinion.
